body.prompt: Industrial design rendering of a compact quadcopter for everyday carry-along aerial photography. Strict orthographic top view, looking straight down, nose toward the top edge, light neutral background. X layout, four motors, one fully unfolded two-blade propeller on each motor, both blades the same length. Fuselage: rounded pebble outline, about 1.6 times as long as wide, widest at mid-body, one unbroken curve. Arm roots: each arm grows out of the shell through a continuous fillet, no joint line. Nose: the camera pod stays inside the nose outline under one continuous rounded leading edge. Top shell: a single cover seam, no vents. A forward-facing camera sits under the nose with its lens pointing forward, so from above only the top of the camera pod shows. Matte light grey shell, dark graphite arms and propellers, no accent colour. Soft even studio light; shading shows the volume. No text, lines or markings. Picture 1 is a top-view plan of the airframe skeleton at the same scale and framing as the output image: four arms and four motor mounts. Keep every motor mount where it is in Picture 1 and run each arm along its bar; arm width and shape are free. The fuselage, the propellers and all other parts are not in the plan; design them from the description. Do not keep the flat grey shapes.
